What exchange rates do to a cross-border budget

An exchange rate is the price of one currency in another.

If a household earns in one currency and spends in another, the same amount can buy more or less when the rate moves.

Hypothetical example: at 50 rupees per Australian dollar, A$200 is 10,000 rupees; at 55 rupees it is 11,000 rupees.

Exchange rates move for many reasons and cannot be predicted reliably. What matters for a budget is knowing the rate you actually received.

Learn. Understand. Stay Informed.
